newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB consortium wins Greek order.
newsitem.headline: ABB consortium wins Greek order.

text.p: ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said a consortium led by the electrical engineering group had won an order valued at $145 million to electrify the 500-km rail link between Piraeus, Athens and Thessaloniki.
The consortium includes Adtranz, the rail venture between ABB and Daimler-Benz AG, ABB said in a statement.
The ABB share of the contract, which was placed by OSE, the Greek State Railways, is around $90 million and Adtranz' share is around $55 million.
Completion of the project is scheduled for 2001.

The project is part of the Greek government's railtrack improvement programme that aims to upgrade key routes to take high-speed trains capable of speeds up to 200 km and to interconnect with the planned trans-European high-speed train network.
ABB will supply and install overhead power supply wires, while Adtranz will supply and install nine trackside substations along the route.
